rows.scope: Persons fatally injured (fatalities include missing persons) in marine occurrences reportable to the TSB under the Canadian Transportation Accident Investigation and Safety Board Act, calendar 2020; the summary itself splits the figure into shipping accidents (14) and accidents aboard ship (4). notes: All 26 rows are counts as printed; nothing is summed by me. Each source counts deaths from ALL causes in reported marine accidents (falls, crushing, fire, drowning, medical events where the source counts them), not drownings, so none can be added to WHO/IHME or national drowning rows. Definitions: (UK) MAIB covers accidents to UK-registered vessels wherever the vessel was and vessels in UK waters; its statistics tables are by vessel type and person (crew on merchant vessels >=100gt: Table 5; passengers: Table 11; fishing vessel crew: Table 22 in the 2023 edition), with no all-vessel yearly series; Annex B of the 2023 report says only Table 1 (the loss-of-life list for the year) includes non-commercial recreational craft. The passenger table gives no definition or vessel coverage sentence; I describe it as printed under the UK merchant vessels >=100gt header. (Canada) TSB counts persons fatally injured, missing persons included, in reportable occurrences on commercial vessels (registered or licensed to operate commercially); pleasure craft occurrences are not normally included unless a commercial vessel was involved; crew and passengers are not separated; shipping accidents and accidents aboard ship are split. (Australia) AMSA counts operational-related fatalities involving a domestic commercial vessel; RAVs and foreign-flagged vessels are reported separately without a series (one seafarer fatality on a foreign-flagged vessel in 2024); recreational vessels are outside the report. Things the reviewer should look at by eye: (1) MAIB 2024 PDF pages 75-94 could not be read; the fishing crew 2024 row (2) rests on the section text and the Chief Inspector's Statement, and the 2019-2023 fishing rows come from the 2023 edition. (2) Revisions between editions: MAIB 2023 edition printed 1 merchant crew death and 2 passenger deaths for 2023; the 2024 edition prints 2 and 3. TSB's 2023 summary printed 7 fatalities for 2022; the 2024 summary prints 9. The rows carry the latest edition's figure and note the earlier one. (3) Zero rows: the MAIB 2024 text layer returned 0 for zero years while the 2023 edition prints a dash; I record the figure as '0'. (4) MAIB page numbers are from the PDF text layer and may be off by one; table numbers and titles are exact. (5) The AMSA web page's '5 fatalities across all vessel types' is not a row: the PDF prints 4 DCV fatalities and, separately, one foreign-flagged seafarer fatality, and I did not combine them. (6) The machine check will warn that some rows equal the sum of two others; with 26 small integers (0-18) that is coincidence, every figure is copied from its table. Grades are A throughout: all figures come from the producing agency's own statistical report or table. ATSB publishes no current yearly marine fatality series that I could find; AMSA is the Australian source. The corrections only add cross-references and a comparability rule to two existing rows; the figures in those rows are unchanged. VERIFICATION 21 Oct 2026: all 26 figures confirmed in the cited tables; MAIB page numbers were one lower than the PDF page markers and have been nudged; 'worldwide' was the contributor's inference and has been softened; pp. 75-94 of the MAIB 2024 PDF remain unread by machine, so the fishing-crew 2024 = 2 row rests on the report's narrative text.
